voiceover.text: Japan is the world's symbol of low birth rates.
But for seven years, Thailand was lower.
In nineteen sixty, a Thai woman had six children on average. A Japanese woman, two.
Thailand's line fell fast. Replacement level in just thirty years.
Then it kept falling, and slipped under Japan in twenty sixteen.
Today, the two are almost tied.
In nineteen ninety, two places had fertility at or below one point three. By twenty twenty-four, twenty-seven.
South Korea. China. Spain. Even Chile.
So where does your country sit? And how fast is it falling?
Find out on Querious. Open the fertility dataset, and write one query.
Then download the result, or connect it to your own tools.
The data is open. The question is yours.
